title: Never Missed a Harvest
lead: The Sundial is growing a third more food than its soil should allow, and Steward Tull won't let the science team below Deck Six. A junior agronomist named Imre Katz slips you a note asking you to come and see the root cellar, and says she'll deny she wrote it.
anyone: The Sundial is growing a third more food than its soil should allow, and Steward Tull won't let the science team below Deck Six. A junior agronomist named Imre Katz has been passing notes about the root cellar, and says she'll deny she wrote them.

gm.truth: In the root cellar below Deck Seven lives Tam Orlo, a nineteen-year-old field hand and a Resonant. A year before the Fall he noticed things grew when he sat with them. Grann found out, and since the Fall he has sat among the soil beds sixteen hours a day, at his own request, more or less. The Sundial's soil is dying, and he's why nobody has noticed: yields are a third higher than those beds can give, which is food for nine thousand people. Resonance always has a price: he's aging. Tam is nineteen and looks forty-five, and he has months. Grann isn't a monster. She comes down every day, reads to him and brings him the first of everything, and she's the only person on the ship who knows what it costs her. His family eats first. He likes it, in a way: "It's the only thing I was ever any good at." He has also started saying that something else is down there when he sits, very slow, under the song. Nobody has asked him what he means.
beats: Katz's note, the locked deck, and soil that, on close inspection, has nothing in it to account for the crop.
The cellar: warm and full of green, an old man who turns out to be nineteen, and a chair with a worn book on it. He's very happy to have a visitor.
Grann catches up. She doesn't deny it or apologize. She asks how many people the captain would like to stop feeding, and to choose them now, since she'll need the names.
An Inquisitor's query arrives, asking in the politest terms about crop yields. Or Katz has told someone else.
The choice. Tam has his own opinion, and he should be asked.
routes: Feel it: attunement to sit with him and see what he's doing. A Resonant captain can take some of the load for a while, at a heavy cost in energy and stress, and learn a lot about the field.
Understand it: science and survival to read the soil and see if any of what he does can be copied by ordinary means. It can, up to about a tenth.
Send for the Order: persuasion to bring Brother Cael, who could teach Tam to draw on the field and not on himself. It's slow, it's uncertain, and word will get out.
Get him out: stealth and piloting to take him off the Sundial, if he agrees. Manifestation can help him let go, since he's holding on very hard.
checks: survival:moderate to see that nothing's been added to the soil and everything's growing anyway
attunement:hard to sit with him and find out what he's giving up
manifestation:very_hard to take the load from him for even a day
science:hard to copy any part of what he does without him
persuasion:very_hard to move Grann Tull on this
stealth:moderate to reach Deck Seven without her family seeing
fights: hegemony_hunter with a warrant, if word reaches the Ministry
outcomes: He stays: the fleet keeps eating, and Tam is close to the end by the year's end. He's content. Grann reads the last chapter aloud, and the next harvest comes up a third short anyway.

He stops: yields drop by a third in two months, and the state of the soil is there for anyone to see. The fleet has to find the food somewhere, and nine thousand people know someone is to blame. Tam, looking forty-five and free, doesn't know what to do with his hands.

Cael teaches him: if it's paid for in time and secrecy, the aging slows but doesn't stop, and the yield settles at fifteen percent over. It's a real compromise, and the Hegemony is now looking at the Sundial.
Exposed: some call Tam a saint, some call Grann a monster and a few call her a hero. A line of hungry people forms to thank him, and Sabine Vael would very much like to meet him.
gm.rewards: A resonance_tuner Tam has been using as a bookmark, Grann's respect or her hatred, and a clue about what lies under the song.
